problems: The coil, the main body, is too small next to the loop. It is narrower (a=0.22) than it is tall, and the three-quarter view squeezes it further, so it reads as a thin oval tag hanging off a big ring. Make the coil round and larger (about 0.3 radius) and the loop a little smaller (R 0.28), so the coil leads the card.

The free inner end runs as a long straight rod through the middle of the coil, from bottom to top. It reads as a strut, not a rope end. Shorten it to a short tail that hangs from the gathered top inside the coil.

The four coil turns are packed so tightly (0.1 total depth for four turns of a 0.022 rope) that they merge into one thick band, so the count does not read. Spread them to about 0.14 and give each turn a slightly different radius so the separate strands show.
Once the coil gets deeper, the red cord's helix radius (0.078) no longer surrounds the bundle. Raise it to about 0.1 so the cord really wraps the coil.
There is a long bare gap of rope between the coil and the honda, which makes a figure-8 silhouette. Bring the knot and loop closer to the coil's right side.

The open loop is no bigger than the coil, so the render reads as a figure-eight or a pair of glasses, not a lasso. A lasso's main feature is a wide loop, clearly larger than the hank. Raise the loop radius from 0.28 to 0.42 so it opens well past the coil.
The honda's free tail is a tiny stub that barely shows. Lengthen it so the end of the rope reads as a real free end.
The red cord's tie-off ends hang loose in the air above the coil. Keep the knot and its short tail close to the wrapped bundle.
